title: Numbers
subtitle: Count things, tell the time, read a price, say your age

rationale.readChoose: Match the Korean to its meaning. The counting word depends on what you are counting.
rationale.listen: Listen for the whole word — neighbouring numbers and sound-alikes are the usual slip.
rationale.nativeSystem: The 하나, 둘, 셋 numbers count things you can point at, and they give the hour and someone’s age.
rationale.sinoSystem: The 일, 이, 삼 numbers are for labels: money, dates, minutes, phone numbers, floors.
rationale.koreanToDigits: Say the parts in order. In the 일, 이, 삼 set, 십 is ten and 삼십 is thirty.
rationale.countingForm: Before a counting word, 하나 둘 셋 넷 스물 become 한 두 세 네 스무. It is 두 개.
rationale.counter: A number never stands beside a noun on its own. The counting word between them depends on what is being counted.
rationale.fill: Read the whole sentence: the words around the gap tell you which form belongs in it.
rationale.nativeBuild: Past ten it is 열 plus the unit — 열하나, 열둘. The tens have their own words.
rationale.sinoBuild: The 일, 이, 삼 numbers are read left to right, part by part: 삼십오 is 삼 · 십 · 오.
rationale.irregular_month: June is 유월 and October is 시월. The regular forms 육월 and 십월 do not exist.
rationale.plain_form: Before a counting word use 한, 두, 세, 네, 스무. 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷 and 스물 do not go there.
rationale.spacing: A counting word is a separate word and takes a space: 한 개, not 한개.
rationale.system_swap: The two sets name the same value but are not interchangeable — the situation decides.
rationale.sound_alike: One sound apart. Listen for the final consonant.
rationale.adjacent: Neighbouring numbers are learned as a list, so they blur. Check the value, not the position.
rationale.wrong_counter: Each counting word belongs to a kind of thing — 명 for people, 마리 for animals, 개 for objects.

systems.title: Saying one to ten
systems.goal: Count to ten two ways, read a nought, and learn when each one is used.

pastTen.title: Numbers bigger than ten
pastTen.goal: Build and read numbers past ten, and learn the five words that change shape when you count.

counting.title: Counting things
counting.goal: Count people, things and animals, and say how old you are.

time.title: What time? What date?
time.goal: Tell the time, and say the date and the day of the week.

money.title: How much? Which number?
money.goal: Read a price, a phone number, a floor, and really big numbers.

review.title: Mistakes people often make
review.goal: Check the five people get wrong most, then put it all together.

sinoBasics.title: Saying 1, 2, 3 in Korean
sinoBasics.objective: Listen to 일, 이, 삼 up to 십, and say them after.
sinoBasics.step1: Korean has two sets of numbers. This set came from Chinese and is used for anything that is a label rather than a count — money, dates, minutes, phone numbers, floors.
sinoBasics.step2: One to ten: 일 이 삼 사 오 육 칠 팔 구 십. Each is one syllable, and each is also a digit you will see on prices and clocks.
sinoBasics.step3: Ten is 십. Everything past ten is built from these ten words, so knowing them well is most of the work.

nativeBasics.title: Counting things: 하나, 둘, 셋
nativeBasics.objective: Listen to 하나 up to 열, say them, and count things in front of you.
nativeBasics.step1: Korea's own numbers. They are used for counting things you can point at — people, cups, animals — and for hours and ages.
nativeBasics.step2: One to ten: 하나 둘 셋 넷 다섯 여섯 일곱 여덟 아홉 열. Notice 여덟 is said 여덜: the ㅂ is silent.
nativeBasics.step3: These stop being used around ninety-nine. Above a hundred, everything is counted with 일, 이, 삼.

zero.title: 0 is 영 or 공
zero.objective: Say 영 for an amount, and 공 when you read a number out.
zero.step1: 영 is zero as an amount — in maths, in a score, in a temperature below zero (영하).
zero.step2: 공 is the digit 0, read aloud in a phone number, a room number, a code. 010 is 공일공, never 영일영.

choosing.title: Which one do I use?
choosing.objective: Choose which numbers to use for counting things, and which for money and dates.
choosing.step1: The 하나, 둘, 셋 numbers count things, up to about ninety-nine: 세 명, 두 시, 스무 살.
choosing.step2: The 일, 이, 삼 numbers are for label-like numbers, money and dates: 오천 원, 삼월 일 일, 삼십 분. Everything above a hundred as well.
choosing.step3: One clock time uses both sets. The hour is 세 시; the minutes are 삼십 분. That pair is the whole rule in miniature. (Books call the two sets native Korean and Sino-Korean. Worth knowing, not worth memorising today.)

sinoBuild.title: Counting to a thousand
sinoBuild.objective: Build and read numbers like 십일, 이십 and 삼십오.
sinoBuild.step1: Say the parts in order. 십일 is ten-one, eleven. 이십 is two-ten, twenty. 삼십오 is three-ten-five, thirty-five.
sinoBuild.step2: Watch 십육: it is written 십육 but said 심뉵. The ㄹ-sound appears between the two syllables.
sinoBuild.step3: 백 is a hundred and 천 is a thousand. There is no 일 in front of them — 백 원, not 일백 원.

nativeBuild.title: Saying 열하나, 스물, 서른
nativeBuild.objective: Say numbers past ten the 하나, 둘, 셋 way.
nativeBuild.step1: 열 plus the unit gives eleven to nineteen: 열하나, 열둘, 열셋. Said as one word.
nativeBuild.step2: The tens have their own words — 스물 twenty, 서른 thirty, 마흔 forty, 쉰 fifty. They are not built from 열.
nativeBuild.step3: 열여섯 is said 열려섣: the same ㄹ-sound that appears in 심뉵.

forms.title: 한 개, 두 개 — the shape changes
forms.objective: When you count, 하나 becomes 한 and 둘 becomes 두. There are five to remember.
forms.step1: Five words change shape in front of a counting word. 하나 becomes 한, 둘 becomes 두, 셋 becomes 세, 넷 becomes 네, 스물 becomes 스무.
forms.step2: This is not a small difference in pronunciation. People say 두 사람, not 둘 사람.
forms.step3: The rest keep their shape: 다섯 명, 여섯 개, 열 마리. Only those five change.

counters.title: 명 for people, 개 for things, 마리 for animals
counters.objective: Count like 세 명, 두 개 and 고양이 두 마리.
counters.step1: Korean never counts a noun with a number alone. Between the number and the thing there is a counting word, chosen by the kind of thing.
counters.step2: 명 counts people (세 명), 개 counts objects (두 개), 마리 counts animals (고양이 두 마리). 사람 also counts people, a little less formally.
counters.step3: The noun comes first, then the number and the counting word: 고양이 두 마리, not 두 마리 고양이.

countersEveryday.title: Two coffees, please
countersEveryday.objective: Order and count in a shop with 병, 잔, 장 and 권.
countersEveryday.step1: 병 is a bottle (맥주 한 병), 잔 is a cup or glass (커피 두 잔), 장 is a flat thing such as a ticket or a sheet (표 네 장), 권 is a book (책 세 권).
countersEveryday.step2: All four take the 하나, 둘, 셋 numbers and their counting forms: 한 병, 두 잔, 세 권, 네 장.

age.title: How old are you?
age.objective: Say your age with 살, and ask an elder politely with 연세.
age.step1: 살 goes with the 하나, 둘, 셋 numbers, and it is what people actually say: 스무 살, 스물다섯 살. 몇 살이에요? asks a friend’s age.
age.step2: 세 goes with the 일, 이, 삼 numbers and turns up in documents and the news: 이십 세. You read it more often than you say it.
age.step3: To someone older, 살 is too casual. 연세 is the honorific word for age: 연세가 어떻게 되세요?

hours.title: What time is it?
hours.objective: Say the hour like 한 시 and 두 시, and use 반 for half past.
hours.step1: The hour takes the 하나, 둘, 셋 numbers: 한 시, 두 시, 세 시, 네 시, 열 시. 몇 시예요? asks the time.
hours.step2: 반 means half: 두 시 반 is half past two. It replaces 삼십 분.
hours.step3: 몇 시예요? asks the hour. Answer like 세 시예요. The minutes use the other set — that is the next lesson.

minutes.title: It's 3:30
minutes.objective: Say minutes and seconds, and join them to the hour.
minutes.step1: Minutes and seconds take the 일, 이, 삼 numbers: 삼십 분, 십오 분, 십 초.
minutes.step2: One clock time uses both sets at once: 세 시 삼십 분 — the hour from 하나, 둘, 셋 and the minutes from 일, 이, 삼.
minutes.step3: It is easy to put both in the same set here. Say 세 시 삼십 분 rather than 삼 시 서른 분.

dates.title: When is your birthday?
dates.objective: Say a date with 년, 월 and 일 — and watch out for 유월 and 시월.
dates.step1: 년, 월 and 일 all take the 일, 이, 삼 numbers: 이천이십육 년 삼월 십오 일. Say the big unit first.
dates.step2: Two months are irregular. June is 유월, not 육월; October is 시월, not 십월.
dates.step3: 일 as a day of the month is the same word as 일 for one. 삼월 일 일 is the first of March.

weekdays.title: What day is it today?
weekdays.objective: Say 월요일 to 일요일, and ask what day it is.
weekdays.step1: The days end in 요일: 월요일 Monday, 화요일, 수요일, 목요일, 금요일 Friday, 토요일, 일요일.
weekdays.step2: 무슨 요일이에요? asks what day it is. 주말 is the weekend.

money.title: How much is it?
money.objective: Read prices like 오천 원 and 만 오천 원.
money.step1: 원 takes the 일, 이, 삼 numbers: 천 원, 오천 원. 얼마예요? asks the price.
money.step2: Korean groups by ten thousand, not by thousand. 만 원 is 10,000; 삼만 오천 원 is 35,000.
money.step3: A price you hear as 만 오천 원 is 15,000 — one ten-thousand and five thousands.

digits.title: Reading a phone number
digits.objective: Read a number one digit at a time, saying 공 for 0 — floors and room numbers too.
digits.step1: A number that identifies rather than counts is read digit by digit: 010 is 공일공.
digits.step2: 에 goes where a dash goes: 공일공에 일이삼사에 오륙칠팔.
digits.step3: Floors, room numbers and bus numbers take the 일, 이, 삼 numbers: 삼 층, 오공이 호, 이백육 번 버스.

large.title: 만, 억 — really big numbers
large.objective: Read big numbers in groups of ten thousand, plus percentages and decimal points.
large.step1: Korean counts in groups of four digits, not three. 만 is ten thousand, 억 is a hundred million, 조 is a trillion.
large.step2: 123,450,000 is read 1억 2345만. Korean groups big numbers by ten-thousands rather than by thousands.
large.step3: 퍼센트 is percent (오십 퍼센트), and 점 is the decimal point: 삼 점 오 is 3.5.

pitfalls.title: Five things people often get wrong
pitfalls.objective: Spot and fix the five that trip people up.
pitfalls.step1: Each of these is a rule you have already met, in the place where it is easiest to forget.
pitfalls.step2: 두 살, not 둘 살. 십육 is said 심뉵. 유월, not 육월. 세 시 for the hour and 삼십 분 for the minutes. A space before the counting word.

mixed.title: Everything, mixed together
mixed.objective: Listen to and read what you have learned, all together.
mixed.step1: This course comes down to one decision made quickly: is this a count or a label? Counts — people, things, hours, ages — take 하나, 둘, 셋; labels — money, minutes, dates, phone numbers — take 일, 이, 삼.
mixed.step2: This review mixes the two. Read or listen, decide, and check the explanation whenever you hesitate. Hesitation is the thing to practise away.

gloss.mixedTime: a clock time, using both sets
gloss.phonePrefix: a phone prefix, digit by digit
gloss.phoneDash: said where a dash is written

gloss.pitfallSpacing: A counting word takes a space
